rejected.note: The article's own title, 'BACKGAMMON.', printed alone on the line. It names the game and states nothing about it; the first rule of the article is the board and the men on p. 271-272, which board-tables, point-designations and starting-position quote.

The Gutenberg edition's placeholder for Fig. 1, '[Illustration: FIG. 1.]'. The figure itself is an image this corpus's text does not contain, which is what the manifest's adapterReach records as illustrations: unsupported. The arrangement it shows is also stated in prose at p. 272 block 4, and that sentence is what starting-position quotes, so nothing rests on the picture alone.

The section title 'PLAYING.', alone on its line. The rules of play it heads -- the throw, the move by pips, doublets, hitting and entering -- are quoted by move-by-pip, doublets, must-play-whole-throw, blot-hit and enter-from-bar.

The section title 'BEARING OFF THE MEN.', alone on its line. Every rule of bearing off is in the paragraphs beneath it, which bearing-off-eligible, bearing-off-move-or-remove, bearing-off-highest, bearing-off-doublets and the stake rules quote.

The edition's placeholder for Fig. 2, '[Illustration: FIG. 2.]', the bearing-off diagram. As with Fig. 1 the image is not in the text this corpus pins, and the bearing-off rules it illustrates are stated in the prose around it.

The section title 'HINTS FOR PLAY.', alone on its line. Excluding this section wholesale as advice is what lost the only authority in this corpus for a die having six faces (#20), so the section is not rejected here -- die-faces quotes its lead-in and the twenty-one throws it enumerates are reached. What is rejected is this line, which is a title.

A ranking of the opening throws: double aces best, then double sixes, then double trois, trois ace and six ace. It obliges nothing and forbids nothing -- 'are reckoned the best' is a judgement about play. Every throw it names is one the enumeration die-faces quotes already prints (ACES, SIXES, DOUBLE TROIS, TROIS ACE, SIX ACE), so no fact about the die rests on this paragraph alone.

Counsel that a throw whose higher number is two in advance of the other is good, because it lets you make a point. The point-making rule itself is stated in the rules of play and quoted there; this says which throws a player should prefer, which is advice under method.md's reading of scope, and cinque trois and trois ace are both in the enumeration die-faces reaches.
The printer's rule '* * * * *' that ends the article. It is a typographic separator of the 1909 edition and carries no words at all.
